originality.rationale: Pointwise closed formula and optimal word for every labeled nonempty subset of each classical Černý automaton, not merely the known two-state distances, all-state threshold, or k-set extremal weight. Behague–Johnson pp.1–4 define the same weight and present extremal comparisons but not this all-subset formula. Related published record titles and substantive summaries treat deficiency, avoidance, or single k-set extremals. Full 2014 Cardoso thesis was not available and remains a specific duplication risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2014 Cardoso dissertation was not available; its detailed Černý subset computations could contain an equivalent expression.
Unindexed or differently phrased literature could give an equivalent max-plus distance function.
Other generic subset-search methods are computationally broader but were compared only for their stated results; absence of a named theorem is not itself novelty proof.

value.rationale: Exact distances and constructive shortest words for every prescribed subset in an extremal synchronizing family form a natural full state-uncertainty metric. This is not the already known pair-only distance or all-state reset time. The max-plus one-step potential is structurally explanatory and gives an O(|S|) evaluation for cyclically ordered S; it supplies new benchmarks and explicit control words for all initial uncertainty sets.
